summary: The new Tenshu commit adds cancellation ownership and a journaled six-phase pairing completion exchange. The main risk surface is the transition after COMMITTED: the current implementation marks the desktop row visible before FINISHED and can roll back an already-recorded decision on drop or non-network failure. Keychain's peer-side lifecycle must also cancel and await pending handlers and derive temporary trust from exact live attempts. The signature-verification boundary itself is unchanged by this commit.
